description: Declared mutants of the net Module, step 1a (docs/architecture/target/v2/net-module-declaration.zh-Hant.md, D-2, D-4, D-12 and judgement G-2; Design Invariants draft in docs/architecture/target/v2/net.zh-Hant.md; ids nt-). A mutant is killed only when the named test case fails with the expected message.

mutants.what: the ack bitfield covers 31 packets instead of 32: the oldest acknowledged packet is left out. Only it catches the width of the bitfield (G-2 still passes, since a later header acknowledges it)
mutants.find:
for (std::uint16_t i = 0; i < 32; ++i) {
            if (WasReceived(static_cast<std::uint16_t>(header.ack - 1 - i))) header.ackBits |= (1u << i);
mutants.replace:
for (std::uint16_t i = 0; i < 31; ++i) {
            if (WasReceived(static_cast<std::uint16_t>(header.ack - 1 - i))) header.ackBits |= (1u << i);
mutants.expect: the\ ack\ bitfield\ covers\ the\ 32\ packets\ before\ ack

mutants.what: an acknowledged packet does not acknowledge the reliable pieces it carried, so they are resent forever. Only it catches the packet-to-piece acknowledgement (G-2 still delivers, with duplicates dropped)
mutants.expect: an\ acknowledged\ piece\ is\ not\ sent\ again

mutants.what: the resend delay ignores the RTT and uses the floor only. Only it catches the 1.5 x RTT term (lightyear ReliableSettings::resend_delay)
mutants.expect: a\ piece\ is\ not\ resent\ before\ 1\.5\ x\ RTT

mutants.what: an Ordered Reliable piece received twice while its message waits behind a gap is counted twice, so the message is never handed out. Only it catches the receiver's piece de-duplication (a duplicate of a message already handed out is caught by the id check before it)
mutants.cases: connection: a reliable piece received twice*
mutants.expect: a\ reliable\ piece\ received\ twice\ is\ handed\ out\ once

mutants.what: an unreliable fragmented message is handed out after its first piece. Only it catches the completeness check of the unreliable reassembly
mutants.expect: an\ incomplete\ fragmented\ message\ is\ not\ handed\ out

mutants.what: a datagram of another connection is accepted. Only it catches the connection id comparison
mutants.cases: connection: a datagram of another connection*
mutants.expect: a\ datagram\ of\ another\ connection\ is\ dropped\ and\ counted

mutants.what: the pieces of an unreliable fragmented message that timed out are dropped without being counted. Only it catches a drop left out of the count (the reconciliation of G-2)
mutants.expect: unreliable\ pieces:\ sent\ \+\ in\ duplicates\ ==\ handed\ out\ \+\ dropped\ \+\ in\ losses

mutants.what: an AckOnly packet asks for an acknowledgement, so two idle ends trade AckOnly packets forever. Only it catches the AckOnly rule (lightyear packet_type.rs:27-37)
mutants.expect: an\ AckOnly\ packet\ does\ not\ ask\ for\ an\ acknowledgement

mutants.what: a packet id already received is processed again, so an unreliable message in a duplicated datagram is handed out twice. Only it catches the packet-level de-duplication
the magic number changes. Only it catches the magic constant of the wire format (README rule 2: one per constant)
mutants.cases: header: the bytes are the documented*
mutants.expect: the\ header\ bytes\ are\ the\ documented\ layout

mutants.what: the protocol version changes without the documented layout changing. Only it catches the version constant (README rule 2: one per constant)
mutants.cases: header: the bytes are the documented*
mutants.expect: the\ header\ bytes\ are\ the\ documented\ layout

mutants.what: a packet kind outside the table (a reserved handshake kind included) is read as Data. Only it catches the closed kind table of the decoder
mutants.cases: header: a datagram that is not a header*
mutants.expect: a\ kind\ outside\ the\ table\ \(a\ reserved\ handshake\ kind\ included\)\ is\ UnknownPacketKind
